organs.name: Heart
organs.blurb: Pumps blood to every part of your body.

parts.name: Right atrium
parts.description: Takes in blood coming back from the body.

parts.name: Right ventricle
parts.description: Pushes that blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen.

parts.name: Left atrium
parts.description: Receives fresh blood returning from the lungs.

parts.name: Left ventricle
parts.description: The strongest chamber. Sends blood to the whole body.

parts.name: Aorta
parts.description: The biggest artery. Carries blood away from the heart.

organs.name: Lungs
organs.blurb: Take in oxygen and let out carbon dioxide.

parts.name: Trachea
parts.description: The windpipe. Carries air down from your throat.

parts.name: Bronchi
parts.description: Two tubes that split air into each lung.

parts.name: Alveoli
parts.description: Tiny air sacs where oxygen enters the blood.

parts.name: Diaphragm
parts.description: The muscle under the lungs that pulls air in.

organs.name: Digestive
organs.blurb: Breaks food down so your body can use it.

parts.name: Oesophagus
parts.description: A tube that squeezes food down to the stomach.

parts.name: Stomach
parts.description: Mixes food with juices that break it apart.

parts.name: Small intestine
parts.description: Takes goodness from food into the blood.

parts.name: Large intestine
parts.description: Takes back water and forms waste.

parts.name: Liver
parts.description: Makes bile and cleans the blood.

organs.name: Brain
organs.blurb: Controls your body and stores what you learn.

parts.name: Cerebrum
parts.description: Thinking, talking and remembering happen here.

parts.name: Cerebellum
parts.description: Keeps you balanced and your movements smooth.

parts.name: Brain stem
parts.description: Controls breathing and heartbeat without you thinking.

parts.name: Spinal cord
parts.description: Carries messages between brain and body.

organs.name: Kidneys
organs.blurb: Clean your blood and make urine.

parts.name: Left kidney
parts.description: Filters waste and extra water out of blood.

parts.name: Right kidney
parts.description: Sits slightly lower, under the liver.

parts.name: Ureter
parts.description: A tube carrying urine down to the bladder.

parts.name: Bladder
parts.description: Stores urine until you go to the toilet.

organs.name: Skeleton
organs.blurb: Holds you up and protects your organs.

parts.name: Skull
parts.description: A bony helmet around the brain.

parts.name: Ribs
parts.description: A cage protecting the heart and lungs.

parts.name: Spine
parts.description: Stacked bones that let you bend and stand.

parts.name: Pelvis
parts.description: Joins your legs to your spine.

parts.name: Femur
parts.description: The thigh bone. The longest bone you have.

heart.title: Two pumps in one
heart.body: The heart is really two pumps side by side. The right side sends blood to the lungs. The left side sends it everywhere else.
heart.definition: One of the four spaces inside the heart that fills with blood and squeezes it out.

heart.title: Where the blood goes
heart.body: Blood leaves the heart through arteries and comes back through veins. One full trip around your body takes about a minute.
heart.definition: A tube that carries blood away from the heart.

heart.title: Valves and beats
heart.body: Valves are small flaps that stop blood flowing backwards. The thump you hear through a stethoscope is valves snapping shut.
heart.definition: A flap that lets blood through one way only.

heart.title: Looking after your heart
heart.body: Running, cycling and swimming make the heart stronger, because it is a muscle. Sleep and water help too.
heart.definition: The beat you can feel in your wrist each time the heart squeezes.

heart.q: Which side of the heart pumps blood to the lungs?
heart.why: The right side sends blood to the lungs to collect oxygen. The left side sends it to the rest of the body.

heart.q: What carries blood away from the heart?
heart.why: Arteries carry blood away. Veins bring it back.

heart.q: How many chambers does a heart have?
heart.why: Two atria on top, two ventricles below.
They are one-way flaps, which is why a heartbeat has two sounds.

heart.q: Roughly how many times a minute does a child’s heart beat at rest?
heart.why: Around 80 to 100 at rest. It slows down as you grow older.

tutor.a: It squeezes about once a second and pushes blood all around you. The blood carries oxygen and food to every cell.
Lungs swap gases. They take oxygen out of the air you breathe in and let out carbon dioxide your body is finished with.

tutor.q: What happens to food after we eat?
tutor.a: It goes down the oesophagus to the stomach, gets mixed with juices, then the small intestine takes the goodness into your blood.
It controls your body and stores what you learn. It also runs things you never think about, like breathing.
Bones hold you up, let you move, and shield soft organs. Your ribs are a cage around your heart and lungs.
